summary: 42 USC 1983: Procedural Due Process — Structural Bias, Denial of Neutral Decisionmaker, Deprivation Without Due Process

counts.title: Count I — 42 U.S.C. § 1983 Damages: Procedural Due Process (14th Amend.) — structural bias; simultaneous prosecutor/adjudicator; irrebuttable presumption of official regularity (against Candelaria, individual capacity)

Count II — 42 U.S.C. § 1983 Declaratory Relief (28 U.S.C. §§ 2201–2202): (a) APS hearing violated Due Process — hearing officer served as DMV's prosecuting advocate and trier of fact; (b) DMV lacked statutory authority — 'lawful arrest' predicate required by VC §§ 13353 and 13353.2 destroyed by PC § 849(b)(1) Detention Certificate; (c) DMV's irrebuttable presumption of official regularity violates procedural due process (against Gordon, official capacity, Ex parte Young)

Count III — 42 U.S.C. § 1983 Injunctive Relief (Ex parte Young): (a) vacate Feb 11 2025 APS Decision Case 34739340; (b) immediate CDL reinstatement free of suspension penalties; (c) prohibit $125 reissue fee and SR-22 requirement; (d) require neutral decisionmaker for any new hearing (against Gordon, official capacity)
